- User (Spencer) identified a gap: leads appearing in Jobber from the website weren't triggering notifications, defeating the original goal of lead-alert automation.

- Claude diagnosed three defects: (1) a 9-hour overnight blind spot (19:00–04:00) in the cron's fixed 3-hour lookback window where zero leads were checked; (2) a faulty "existing customer" rule that filtered legitimate Jobber leads with addresses; (3) the alert ignored Jobber's `leadSource` field and guessed source from record shape instead.

- Five leads were dropped silently: Leslie Postovoit (website, Aug 6, 8:17 PM), Jay Hickenbottom (Google/referral, Aug 5), Mo Brown (Google, Aug 5), Dick Keiser (Google, Aug 5), Maryanne Zukowski (Google, Aug 5). Two others partially caught via Thumbtack's own emails.

- Fixes implemented: look-back now stretches to last successful run (capped 36h), `leadSource` field overrides skip rule, source line now clearly shows "Website form", "Phone — CallRail", "Thumbtack", or referral partner name.

- User requested an audit to identify how many open Quick Fix jobs in Jobber had exceeded five weekly visits.
- Claude Code swept all 817 live jobs in Jobber, classified product by line item (not jobType), and identified 117 open Quick Fix jobs.
- Audit found **11 open Quick Fix jobs past the 5-visit threshold**: 10 with genuine 7-day gaps, 1 commercial account (#7964 Barbee Mill HOA) running 28-day intervals and misclassified as Quick Fix.
- Key findings: 31+ extra visits already delivered beyond the purchased 5-week series; all 11 overrun jobs have additional visits already booked; 60 total visits scheduled past week 5 across the full Quick Fix portfolio; 9 more jobs will cross the 5-visit line within 7 days; combined program value of overrun jobs is $5,100.
- Root cause identified: the cadence engine was designed to **flag** Quick Fix jobs at visit 5 for a human sales decision (extend, sell TMCP, close), but the recurring series in Jobber auto-generates weekly visits regardless, creating no gate or escalation prompt.
- Only 1 of 117 Quick Fix jobs stopped cleanly at 5 visits (#8151 Chuck Blevens), showing the current system is not blocking overruns.
